transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess what finally scared me enough to make the appointment is that I’ve been having these thoughts that it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up. Not like— I don’t know, it feels awful to even say it out loud. But it’s been there, more than I’m comfortable admitting.

And sometimes when I’m driving home from the clinic, after a long day, I catch myself thinking… what would happen if I just didn’t turn the wheel. It’s not something I want to be thinking, and it scares me that my mind even goes there. That’s why I’m here.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once looked forward to?

Yes. Very much, actually. That’s been one of the things that scares me, because it’s not just being “too busy” or forgetting for a weekend. I haven’t touched my camera in… I don’t even know how long, and photography used to be one of the ways I paid attention to the world, if that makes sense.

And I have bird feeders outside, and I used to check them constantly—what birds were coming through, whether the seed needed changing, whether the little finches were back. Now I’ll see them out there and it’s like I know I should care, but I just… don’t feel anything about it. Same with the garden. Normally I’d be thinking ahead, planning what’s coming up, noticing what’s blooming or what needs tending, but lately I can barely make myself look at it.

Those things used to be how I felt like myself. So losing interest in them feels frightening, like I’m watching myself disappear a little.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past couple of weeks?

Yes. I mean… yes, that’s exactly what it’s been like. Most days, from the time I’m up and moving around, it feels like the color has just drained out of everything. Like the house can be busy, people around, normal sounds happening, laundry going, dishes, whatever ordinary life is supposed to be… and I’m there, but I’m not really there.

It’s this heavy, hopeless feeling that just sits on me. And I try not to show it, because I don’t want everyone looking at me like something is wrong, or asking questions I don’t know how to answer. So I’ll go into the laundry room and pretend I’m switching loads or folding towels, and then I just… cry. Quietly, because I can’t stand the thought of anyone seeing me like that. It’s embarrassing, but also more than embarrassing. It feels like if they saw how hopeless I really feel, it would make it real in a way I’m not ready for.

So yes, most of the day, most days. It’s not just a bad afternoon here and there. It’s been there a lot.
Have you been feeling like you’re a burden to others, or been struggling with guilt or shame about things you’ve done—or haven’t done—recently?

Yes… yes, I have. A lot.

It’s embarrassing to say, but I keep getting stuck on this thought that I’m just… a terrible person. Especially at home. There’s been disruption and stress in the house, and instead of being patient or grateful or whatever I’m supposed to be, I catch myself feeling resentful. And then I hate myself for feeling that way. I’ll think, what kind of person resents their own family needing things, or resents the house not being calm, or gets irritated when everyone is just trying to get through their day?

And then I replay everything. Like, if I gave my husband an impatient look, or if my tone got sharp, or if I answered someone too quickly—my mind keeps pulling it back up later like it’s evidence. Not just, “Oh, I was tired and could have handled that better,” but more like, “See? This is who you really are. You’re selfish. You make everything harder.”

It turns into this whole loop where I think my husband and the family would honestly be better off without me around making the mood heavier, or snapping, or quietly resenting things. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but in the moment it feels completely true. Like I’m not contributing anything good, just taking up space and making people deal with me.
Have you ever felt this way before, with similar feelings of depression or loss of interest, or has this been a new experience for you?

It’s not completely new, no. I mean, I’ve had low periods before, but this particular depression has been hanging over me for a long time now—about 11 months, if I’m trying to be honest about it.

At first I kept telling myself it was just a phase, or stress, or that I was tired and would bounce back once things settled down. So I didn’t really mark it as “this is depression” right away. It was more like this grayness slowly settled in and just… stayed. And then this past month, it’s like everything got turned up to an unbearable level. The hopelessness, the not caring about things, the feeling like I can’t get back to myself—it all became much harder to ignore.

So no, it didn’t just start recently, but the last month has made it feel much more frightening and much harder to function around.
Have you had other times in your life when you felt this way, with periods of depression that were similar or maybe even less severe than what you're experiencing now?

I’m… not sure how to answer that cleanly. I don’t want to say no, because I’ve definitely had times in my life where I’ve felt low or kind of flattened out, where things felt harder than they should have. But I also don’t know that I’ve always recognized it at the time as the same thing, if that makes sense.

Looking back, there were periods where I withdrew more, or everything felt like too much, or I just sort of pushed through because that’s what you do. I’m not sure I could give you neat start and stop dates, or say, “Yes, that was exactly like this.” This one feels… bigger. Heavier. More consuming. So I can’t confidently say how similar the older times were, but I do think this isn’t the first time I’ve had a version of feeling really down for more than just a bad day or two.

I’m sorry, that’s probably not a very precise answer. It’s hard to sort out what was normal stress or exhaustion and what was something more than that.
Can you recall if there were clear periods in your life when you felt better for a while—like a few months or more—between the times you felt down or depressed?

I’m not sure I can remember it clearly enough to say. That’s part of what’s hard for me—I can look back and remember being “okay” in stretches, or at least functioning, but I don’t know if that means I truly felt better or if I was just busier, distracted, or managing better.

A few months or more… I mean, probably? There must have been periods where I wasn’t feeling this weighed down every day, because I did have times where life felt more normal. But I can’t pull it into a clean pattern in my head, like, “I was depressed here, then fine for six months, then depressed again.” It all feels kind of blurred together when I try to remember it now.

I can say there were times I wasn’t consumed by it the way I am now. But whether those were clear, sustained “better” periods, I don’t know. I’m sorry—I feel like I keep giving you vague answers, but I don’t want to make it sound more definite than it really is in my memory.
Can you recall if there was ever a time when you felt clearly better for several months or more, where you were not struggling with these depressive feelings on a daily basis?

I’m trying to think, and I wish I had a cleaner answer. I don’t really remember a clearly defined stretch like that in a way I’d feel confident telling you, “Yes, there were several months where I was definitely not dealing with it.” I can remember times where I seemed more normal from the outside, I guess—going to work, keeping up with responsibilities, having days where I wasn’t thinking about how awful everything felt all the time—but when I try to look back, it’s hard to tell whether I was actually better or just coping better.

There may have been months where it wasn’t daily, or at least not as loud every day. But I don’t know if that counts as clearly better. My memory of it is kind of smeared together, especially now that I’m in it so deeply. It’s like I can remember the general tone of different periods, but not with enough precision to say, “That was a real break from it.”

So… I don’t want to say no, because maybe there were times like that. But I also can’t honestly say yes in a definite way. I just don’t know.
